As of October 2025, Arizona had approximately 4.5 million active registered voters:
Republicans: ~1,603,000 (35.6%)
Democrats: ~1,270,000 (28.2%)
Others/Independents: ~34.4%
This gives Republicans a lead of over 330,000 voters. Earlier in 2025:
July: Republicans ~1,598,000 (35.7%), Democrats ~1,270,000 (28.4%)
August: Republicans ~1,577,000 (35.6%), Democrats ~1,262,000 (28.5%)
Reports confirm that Republican registrations hit an all-time high above 1.6 million in late 2025, while Democratic numbers have dropped by roughly 108,000 since 2020, with Republicans holding steady or growing modestly.
This trend has widened the GOP advantage since the 2020-2024 period, when Democratic shares fell from around 33% to 29%, and the Republican edge expanded significantly. Independents remain the largest group in raw numbers in some snapshots, but Republicans maintain the partisan lead.
Note that no official December 2025 figures from the Arizona Secretary of State were available in the searched data, but mid-to-late 2025 reports show a consistent pattern favoring Republican growth relative to Democrats. Voter registration can fluctuate, and independents often play a decisive role in elections.
